messages.subject: Factor variable and random slope
parts:
Hi there, I'm running into a problem regarding random slopes for a factor variable with five levels. I am trying to extract the posterior random slopes for each level of the factor. My question is, is that even possible?
The formula is here:
formula= TermLBW~as.factor(no2.cut)+female+f(FIPS2, as.factor(no2.cut), model="iid")

result= inla(formula, family="binomial", data=bo.dat, control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, return.marginals=TRUE)).

Thanks so much!

Best
Eric

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Factor variable and random slope
parts:
It does not make sense to have
f(id, as.factor(x), model='iid')
because the second argument in f() must be numeric

Also, I think that
y ~ factor(x)
is more or less the same as
y ~ f(x, model='iid')
So, by having
y ~ factor(x) + f(x, model='iid')
we have a redundancy and identification problem as well.

You can see that
inla(y ~ factor(x))$summary.fix
is similar to
inla(y ~ f(x, model='iid'))$summary.random$x
